articles.title: Travis Hunter sets the internet on fire with his dancing ability while catching footballs
articles.summary: Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars lost 34-17 to the Carolina Panthers in a 2026 Preseason Week 2 game at EverBank Stadium, Travis Hunter set the internet on fire with his dance moves while catching footballs.
articles.body:
Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars lost 34-17 to the Carolina Panthers in a 2026 Preseason Week 2 game at EverBank Stadium, Travis Hunter set the internet on fire with his dance moves while catching footballs.

The former Heisman Trophy winner didn’t get to play, but fans were loving the show he put on while being at the sidelines.

Despite the loss, there was a strong showing early for the Jaguars Friday: the play of rookie wide receivers CJ Williams and Josh Cameron, a pair of sixth-round '26 selections who have impressed throughout training camp and the preseason.

articles.title: Travis Hunter’s biggest allies in Jacksonville’s championship pursuit could be two wideout rookies
articles.standfirst: The newcomers have shown ability and speed that can give defenses nightmares
articles.summary: The newcomers have shown ability and speed that can give defenses nightmares
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars may have suffered a 34-17 preseason loss to the Carolina Panthers on Friday night, but the final score was not the most important takeaway from EverBank Stadium. Instead, some of the most encouraging developments came from two rookies who continue to build momentum heading toward the regular season.

Wide receivers CJ Williams and Josh Cameron , both selected in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft , once again flashed the potential that has made them two of the most talked-about young players in J acksonville's training camp. And if their development continues, they could become valuable allies for superstar rookie Travis Hunter as the Jaguars attempt to build a roster capable of competing for a championship.

Hunter entered the NFL with enormous expectations. As one of the most dynamic prospects in recent memory, his ability to impact games in multiple ways has generated excitement throughout Jacksonville. But even generational talents need support, and the Jaguars may have found two unexpected contributors who can help lighten the load. Against Carolina, both Williams and Cameron continued their impressive preseason performances.

Depth often determines whether a season ends in January or February

Cameron hauled in two receptions for 41 yards during the first half, showcasing the big-play ability that has consistently appeared throughout camp. Williams , meanwhile, recorded four catches for 22 yards, continuing to demonstrate reliability and route-running precision. Neither performance will dominate national headlines, but inside the Jaguars' building, the contributions have not gone unnoticed.

Head coach Liam Coen offered strong praise for both rookies after the game, highlighting not only their on-field production but also the professional habits that have accelerated their development. That type of endorsement carries significant weight, especially for late-round draft picks fighting to establish themselves on an NFL roster.

For championship contenders, depth often determines whether a season ends in January or February. Teams that can consistently uncover contributors beyond the first few rounds of the draft gain a significant advantage, particularly when injuries inevitably test a roster's depth. The Jaguars appear hopeful that Williams and Cameron can become those kinds of players.

Defenses could find themselves facing difficult decisions

Both receivers have earned attention throughout training camp by consistently making plays, understanding the offensive system, and displaying maturity beyond their years. Their strong work ethic has translated into opportunities during preseason action, and they have capitalized on those chances.

That development could prove especially important for Hunter. As Jacksonville continues integrating its highly touted rookie into the offense, opposing defenses will inevitably devote considerable attention to slowing him down. The emergence of additional receiving threats would make that task far more difficult.

If Williams and Cameron continue progressing, defenses could find themselves facing difficult decisions. Focus too heavily on Hunter, and the rookie receivers may exploit favorable matchups. Shift attention elsewhere, and Travis could take over games with his unique playmaking ability. That is how dangerous offenses are built.

articles.title: Travis Hunter stunned as police make major drug bust during ride-along
articles.summary: Travis Hunter got an unexpected look at police work during a recent ride-along with Jacksonville Sheriff T.K. Waters, when officers showed the Jaguars star a bag of drugs allegedly recovered during a traffic stop.
articles.body:
Travis Hunter got an unexpected look at police work during a recent ride-along with Jacksonville Sheriff T.K. Waters, when officers showed the Jaguars star a bag of drugs allegedly recovered during a traffic stop.

The bust reportedly involved marijuana, meth, suspected cocaine and fentanyl, leaving Hunter stunned before he joked that police had caught a “kingpin” and warned kids to stay away from drugs.

The NFL star is preparing for his second season with the Jaguars after appearing in just seven games as a rookie, but after witnessing the dramatic bust firsthand, it seems he may have a future in law enforcement if football ever takes a back seat.

articles.title: Jacksonville Jaguars: Here’s how the new uniform pays tribute to the city
articles.standfirst: The Jaguars’ new design changes their look for the 2026 season.
articles.summary: The Jaguars’ new design changes their look for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have a new look for the 2026 season. The team, along with Nike and the NFL, unveiled its “Bold City Glow” rivalry uniform, a design that moves away from the franchise’s usual color combination in favor of a different aesthetic and, above all, one that is much more connected to Jacksonville.

The new uniform features a color that is different from the shade that typically defines the team: a cream color inspired by Florida’s coastal culture. It is paired with the word “Jaguars” in a cursive font and numbers that combine matte and glossy finishes . The outside of the collar also features the inscription “Since '95,” referring to the year the franchise was founded.

However, the most striking and significant change appears on the head. For the first time in franchise history, the Jaguars will wear a shiny teal helmet, complete with a gold face mask and the regional “904” mark.

But the changes and the connection to Jacksonville do not end there.

What is hidden in the Jaguars’ new uniform?

The pants feature a black base with a subtle jaguar-spot pattern, along with a teal stripe outlined in gold. However, the pattern hides a detail that directly connects the uniform to the city .

Hidden among the spots are the names of different Jacksonville neighborhoods, incorporated into the design as a tribute to the communities that are part of the city’s identity .

When will the Jaguars debut the new uniform?

Although the design has already been unveiled, fans will have to wait to see it in an official game. The Jaguars will debut the uniform in Week 8, on November 1, 2026, when they host the Indianapolis Colts, one of their division rivals .

Jacksonville finished the 2025 season with a 13-4 record, won the AFC South , and closed the regular season with eight consecutive victories. However, their run ended in the Wild Card Round with a 27-24 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Now, the new uniform marks the beginning of another chapter for the franchise, but its meaning goes beyond the football field.
